section_summary: This section continues a report on Japan’s whaling industry, then turns to Japanese fishing activity in Costa Rican, Philippine, Argentine and North Pacific waters. Reports and correspondence describe fishing fleets, licensing disputes, suspected espionage and wartime concerns. The final documents consider Japanese salmon and crab fisheries near Kamchatka and proposals to disrupt them.

subfiles.title: Report on the Japanese whaling industry, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Describes Japan’s growing Antarctic whaling fleet and uses of whale products.
subfiles.summary: The report traces rapid growth in Japanese factory ships, catchers, whale catches and oil production during the 1930s. It describes whaling grounds, export markets and new domestic uses of meat, hide, viscera and oil.

subfiles.title: Suspicious activities of Japanese fishing vessel Amano
subfiles.about: Reports suspected transfers from a Japanese merchant vessel to the Amano off Costa Rica.
subfiles.summary: Reports an alleged high-seas transfer of heavy containers to the Amano and possible related coastal unloading.

subfiles.title: Letter on Japanese whaling boats in pack ice
subfiles.about: Thanks Sturgeon for an article extract and comments on Japanese whaling boats abandoned in pack ice.
subfiles.summary: Kellogg describes reports of three stranded catchers, one later recovered.

subfiles.title: Philippine Affairs routing sheet
subfiles.about: Records receipt and filing of Philippine Affairs material.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible receipt and filing marks.

subfiles.title: Counselor’s note on Sayre’s letter
subfiles.about: Introduces Sayre’s assessment of Japanese fishing in Philippine coastal waters.
subfiles.summary: Sayre considers Philippine enforcement capacity inadequate and fears stricter action could worsen the situation.

subfiles.title: Philippine Affairs note on O’Rear report
subfiles.about: Refers readers to Sayre’s letter and the military intelligence report.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten routing note referring to Sayre and O’Rear.

subfiles.title: Sayre’s letter to Jacobs on Japanese fisheries
subfiles.about: Explains why effective enforcement of Philippine fishing laws against Japanese operators would be difficult.
subfiles.summary: Sayre says Philippine officials know of violations but lack vessels, trained fishermen and reliable local enforcement. He warns that a crackdown might heighten Philippine-Japanese tensions without improving the fishery.

subfiles.title: Aquino’s report on Philippine fisheries
subfiles.about: Reviews Philippine fishery development, enforcement and conservation needs.
subfiles.summary: Aquino describes prosecutions of unlicensed fishing, conservation orders, landing rules, research stations and administrative changes. He asks for patrol resources and a training ship to develop Filipino deep-sea fishing skills.

subfiles.title: Sturgeon’s memorandum on Japanese fishing in Philippine waters
subfiles.to: R. Moore and Far Eastern Affairs colleagues
subfiles.about: Summarizes a military intelligence report on Japanese dominance and alleged espionage in Philippine fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Sturgeon highlights Japanese market control, unlicensed fishermen, Filipino registration fronts, dynamite fishing and intelligence concerns.

subfiles.title: Jacobs’s note to Moore
subfiles.about: Reports a conversation with Colonel Bratton about whether Sayre saw the fishing report.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs plans to draw Sayre’s attention to the report.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck routing slip
subfiles.about: Requests Sturgeon’s comment on attached material.
subfiles.summary: Asks Sturgeon to telephone with any comment.

subfiles.title: Handwritten return note
subfiles.about: Routes attached material for return after reading.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten request to return the material.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fisheries in Philippine Waters
subfiles.doc_type: confidential military intelligence report with vessel register and map
subfiles.from: J. T. H. O’Rear, Philippine Department
subfiles.to: Assistant Chief of Staff, War Department
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese fishing interests, alleged unlawful activity and vessels in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: The report describes Japanese fishing firms, methods, crews, markets and alleged smuggling and espionage. It claims widespread licensing violations and Filipino nominal ownership, then lists nearly 200 boats with registered owners, specifications and license numbers. A map of the Philippines closes the report.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser’s forwarding memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards an FBI report about Japanese fishermen on the United States Pacific coast.
subfiles.summary: Calls attention to population and fishing-boat figures in the attached report.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Japanese fishermen at Terminal Island
subfiles.about: Discusses Japanese fishing residents, boats and proposed changes affecting Terminal Island.
subfiles.summary: Reports concern over Terminal Island’s future and counts Japanese residents and fishing craft.

subfiles.title: Japanese government negotiations for Argentine trawlers
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese negotiations to buy five Argentine fishing trawlers.
subfiles.summary: Hughes describes talks with Pesquerías Gardella, considers possible uses of the vessels and notes the Argentine and British governments’ apparent lack of interest. An enclosure lists fourteen trawlers and their dimensions, tonnage and power.

subfiles.title: Recent Developments in Japan’s Marine Products Industry
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed fishing-firm merger, a poor salmon catch and growing frozen-shellfish exports.
subfiles.summary: Lamm describes plans to merge bonito and tuna firms amid fuel and supply shortages. He also reports a reduced salmon catch, export stockpiles and domestic shortages, plus expanding exports of frozen clams and scallops.

subfiles.title: Transmission of clipping on Japanese Bering Sea fishing
subfiles.about: Forwards a newspaper item on Japanese cod fishing and converted floating canneries in the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Chase sends a Hakodate news report that might not have reached other American offices.

subfiles.title: North Sea fishery ships depart for this year’s catch
subfiles.about: Reports departures for northern fishing grounds and conversion of crab canneries to cod canneries.
subfiles.summary: Names departing vessels and expected fishing near the Kurils, Kamchatka and Bering Sea.

subfiles.title: Tydings’s letter on Japanese fishing-crew replacements
subfiles.about: Passes on a constituent’s allegations that Japanese merchant crews replace fishing crews for espionage.
subfiles.summary: The constituent alleges covert crew exchanges, unusual voyages and a portable radio used from a Channel Island. The claims are presented as secondhand information.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Sends Tydings’s allegations to military intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Tydings’s letter for military intelligence information.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Tydings
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the allegations about Japanese fishing crews.
subfiles.summary: Says the matter is being referred to investigative agencies.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter to Attorney General
subfiles.about: Refers Tydings’s letter to the FBI and immigration authorities.
subfiles.summary: Requests appropriate action on the alleged crew replacements.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Sends Tydings’s letter to naval intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the allegations for naval intelligence information.

subfiles.title: Report on fishing vessel Amano’s crew
subfiles.to: Acting Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2
subfiles.about: Reports that Amano’s non-Japanese captain left the vessel.
subfiles.summary: Christian Albertssen’s departure leaves the Amano apparently entirely Japanese crewed.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: arrest of Japanese fishing boats in Mexico
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on two boats arrested for violating Mexican law.
subfiles.summary: References despatch 14604 in another file.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Yoshino and Ryono
subfiles.about: Points to a report on Japanese fishing boats Yoshino and Ryono.
subfiles.summary: References despatch 14625 in another file.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on control of Japanese fishermen off Mexico
subfiles.about: Relays discussions with Mexico about restricting Japanese fishing off its west coast.
subfiles.summary: Officials discussed keeping Japanese fishermen ashore or issuing individual certificates to those allowed to fish. Colonel Thomason expected a mixed solution and promised to relay Mexico’s decision.

subfiles.title: Note on Navy review of Japanese fisheries file
subfiles.about: Records Captain Schuirman’s review of memoranda on Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Schuirman read the file and said the Navy was considering the matter.

subfiles.title: Cover note on fisheries and submarine proposal
subfiles.about: Explains the attached analysis responding to Adams’s proposal about Japanese fishing fleets.
subfiles.summary: Describes Adams’s suggestion and its proposed transmission to the Navy.

subfiles.title: Comment on Japanese fishery resources and operating areas
subfiles.about: Assesses Japanese northern fisheries as possible targets of economic warfare.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum weighs reported food shortages against Japan’s extensive fisheries and former export production. It identifies fishing and canning areas around Hokkaido, the Kurils, Kamchatka and the Sea of Okhotsk, while noting limited current intelligence and possible retaliation against Alaskan fisheries.

subfiles.title: Adams’s proposal concerning Japanese fishing fleets
subfiles.from: Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Suggests studying whether submarines could curtail Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Adams cites reported fish shortages and proposes a Navy and fisheries survey. He also speculates about underwater detonations and notes a Johannesburg despatch on Kamchatka salmon.

subfiles.title: Copy of Adams’s fisheries proposal
subfiles.from: Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Duplicates the proposal to study interference with Japanese fishing fleets.
subfiles.summary: Copy of Adams’s memorandum, with the note on Kamchatka salmon.

subfiles.title: Johannesburg transmittal on Kamchatka salmon fishing
subfiles.about: Encloses Consul Wright’s memorandum on Japanese salmon fishing in Kamchatka.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Wright’s account for diplomatic distribution.

subfiles.title: Salmon Fishing on the Kamchatka Peninsula
subfiles.about: Records A. J. Hartman’s account of Japanese salmon fishing along Kamchatka.
subfiles.summary: Hartman describes the brief July salmon run, small shore boats supplying larger processing ships, west-coast fishing and canning near the Kamchatka River mouth. He argues that disrupting the fishery would damage Japan’s war effort.

subfiles.title: Department of State return slip
subfiles.about: Directs return of the file or attached material.
subfiles.summary: Return instruction with receipt stamps.
